questions.stem: What is the key difference between ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption?

options.text: Ultrafiltration occurs in the liver; selective reabsorption occurs in the kidneys
Ultrafiltration uses active transport; selective reabsorption uses diffusion only
Ultrafiltration produces urine; selective reabsorption produces urea
Ultrafiltration removes all small molecules from the blood; selective reabsorption returns useful ones

questions.explanation: Ultrafiltration non-selectively forces all small molecules out of the blood in the glomerulus. Selective reabsorption then returns useful substances like glucose and amino acids to the blood, while waste products like urea remain in the filtrate.
